Representative Kulm and esteemed colleagues on the Committee on Judiciary, I am Senator
Anne Carney, proudly representing Senate District 29, which includes South Portland, Cape
Elizabeth and part of Scarborough. It is a pleasure to be with you today to introduce LD 248, "An Act to Rename the Administrator of the Office of Chief Medical Examiner the Director of
Medical Examiner Operations."
This is a department bill from the Office of Chief Medical Examiner. A representative from their
office will follow me to present more specifics, and I invite you to direct your questions to them.
Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to introduce this bill.

Re: LD 248
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and members of the committee,
I am Lindsey Chasteen, the Office Administrator for the Office of Chief Medical Examiner (OCME). I
am speaking today on LD 248, An Act to Rename the Administrator of the Office of Chief Medical
Examiner the Director of Medical Examiner Operations. The Office Administrator position was established in 1997 and was responsible for the daily "behind-the-scenes" of the agency. As the office has grown, so have the responsibilities.
Per statute (Chap. 7ll �3022(2-A)) this position "shall perform such duties as may be delegated by the
Chief Medical Examiner" . The current job description is a broken hyperlink to the statute. Over the years,
H
this position has become the equivalent of a Director, responsible for creating/managing the budget, hiring/discipling, vetting vendors, managing contracts, being the media liaison, and working with outside
agencies. In an office with l2 other staff (11 FTE and l grant funded), this position directly, or indirectly
supervises 10 of those people.
LD 248 looks to change the current title of "Office Administrator" to "Director of Medical Examiner
Operations" to better capture the responsibilities of the role, and make clear that this role is within the Medical Examiner's Office.

Thank you for your consideration.
